classification.difficultyReason: Students identify A as the starting point, recognise AB as due south and add the marked 34 degrees to 180 degrees to obtain the clockwise bearing.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows the positions of towns A, B and C.

What is the true bearing of Town C from Town A?

spec.description: A vertically above B, with C southwest of A and above B. All three town connections, point markers, north arrow and given angle are retained. Coordinates express the given angle; segment lengths are illustrative and are not printed givens.
spec.mathematics: The angle between south from A and AC is 34 degrees, so AC has bearing 214 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 34-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
North to south is $180^{\circ}$. Therefore the bearing of C from A is
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Bearing}&=180^{\circ}+34^{\circ}\\&=214^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
